proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (~5 eV), electronically insulating, Li-rich phosphate that is a well-known LiCoO2 coating. Its Li-rich oxyanion chemistry should give low interfacial reactivity with the sulfide electrolyte and good stability near 4 V, which favors a small interface penalty.

Li3NbO4 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating oxide with Nb5+ in a fully oxidized octahedral environment. Its high lithium content and oxide-only anion chemistry should limit reactive exchange with the sulfide electrolyte near 4 V, which may give a lower contact penalty than the phosphate tested earlier.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) was insulating and wide-gap but gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom from P/S/Cl redox products, so a different oxide family with a Li-rich, high-valent cation is worth testing.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, fully reduced oxide with no high-valent cation to be reduced. Its O2- and Li+ ions are already at their stable oxidation states, so it should have few reactive pathways with the sulfide electrolyte, unlike the P5+ and Nb5+ coatings tested so far, which formed P/S/Cl or Nb redox products on contact.

Its Al3+ should resist reduction by Li6PS5Cl near 4 V, unlike the P5+ and Nb5+ coatings that formed P/S/Cl or Nb reduction products.
